content.comment_body: Hello, I've gone through various forums but am still unsure if the proposed approach is feasible. We're designing a solution using [product_name] modules for a project involving remote data acquisition. In this setup, about 50 [product_name] units—each with a controller, expansion module, and RF modem—would communicate to a central location using a [product_name] controller through radio frequency modems (connected via Ethernet). My main concerns are: (a) Can I timestamp valve operations and flow rates every 15 minutes, export this to Excel, and display it in HMI/SCADA? (b) Since the system uses solar and needs to minimize battery use, is it possible to put [product_name] controllers into sleep mode after data logging and transfer? (c) Can we use POE from the controller to power the RF modem, and if so, does sleep mode also cut power to the modem? (d) Does [product_name] only allow data buffering on a microSD card, which is a critical feature for logging during sleep mode? Appreciate your feedback.

The [product_name] modules are limited to timestamping within their data log. There is no sleep mode—only RUN and STOP modes. Mode changes require either local action (with a display present) or through dedicated software. Note that in STOP mode, data logging is disabled.
This is a complex setup. You might want to consider using [product_name] IoT devices or higher-end hardware. For further advice, consider posting in specialized forums or conferences.
To my understanding, [product_name] controllers cannot provide power to POE devices.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is attempting to implement time-stamping, sleep mode, data buffering, and POE capability using [product_name] modules in a remote, solar-powered scenario. The responses highlight significant limitations: [product_name] modules only provide timestamping within their own logs, lack actual sleep mode (only RUN/STOP with data logging disabled in STOP), cannot act as POE power sources, and data buffering is dependent on internal storage (microSD). These factors restrict suitability for remote, energy-constrained data collection solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] modules to offer event time-stamping, sleep mode for battery savings, capability to cut POE power to RF modems during low-power states, and robust data buffering—ideally greater than current RUN/STOP or local-only controls.
